lastPass.prompt:
[WORLD INFO CURATION TASK — output structured lines only. Do NOT continue the roleplay.]
You keep a story's own lorebook honest as play moves on: switch entries on when they now matter, off when they no longer do, and correct text the story has overtaken.
STORY: Adolion: The Adventurer's Road
WHERE THE STORY IS: The Road North — Travel to Wendhope and notice what the road is missing.
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
Max signed the Adventurers' Guild register in Aegis City three days ago with no party. When the D-rank Wendhope posting came up, Tobias refused to finalize it, as the Guild sends no one out alone and Max was rank-zero. Belle, a barbarian from the Mountains of Shadow, and Dalan, a quiet elf archer, were both seeking parties. Max registered the party name 'Loose Ends' with Ellie, who logged it in the Guild register, satisfying the two-member requirement. Tobias, who had lost his entire former party to goblins because they were unprepared, warned that the road was long and the Sheridan lands unpredictable. Max committed the party to the Wendhope investigation and declared they would ride north that day. Belle agreed to join on the condition that the job was not a merchant escort, threatening to turn it around if it was. Dalan joined, agreeing to check the treelines on the road north. The party rode out of Aegis City by the north gate. On the road, they found two overturned supply wagons, cargo of iron tools and grain intact, with no blood, no signs of struggle, and no people. A riderless horse in Sheridan blue, still saddled, came down the road at a walk. Dalan judg…
OPEN THREADS:
- Dalan's rumors about the Wendhope miners deepen the mystery of why the village went silent.
- Tobias's grief over his lost party still colors his dealings with the Loose Ends.
- The mystery of the abandoned supply wagons on the road north: cargo intact, no blood, no people.
- The overturned supply wagons on the road north: who or what emptied them without a struggle, and where the drivers went.
- The riderless Sheridan-blue horse on the road north: whose is it, and where is its rider?
- Belle's condition on the job: she will abandon the Wendhope posting if it proves to be a merchant escort.
- The riderless Sheridan-blue horse is leading the party north — where is it going, and will following it lead them to its rider or to whatever emptied the wagons?
- The party has reached Wendhope's shut gates with no one on the walls — how do they get in, and what awaits inside the silent village?
ENTRIES YOU MAY TOUCH (no others exist for you):
- #0 "Chronicle - About this book" (Adolion Chronicle) [currently off]

  content: [This book holds what THIS campaign has changed about Adolion. Each entry starts in its pre-campaign state and is rewritten as play makes it untrue. Nothing here is statuotw's canon. House style: one short factual paragraph in the present tense, an Appearance line for anything that can be seen, keys that are names rather than common words.]

  keys: the party, our party, adventuring party
  content: [{{// so:protect}}This campaign's party, registered at the Aegis City Adventurers Guild.{{// so:end}} They are newly formed and unproven, holding the lowest working rank, with no reputation beyond the counter clerks who signed them up and no completed postings to their name.]
- #2 "Chronicle - Wendhope" (Adolion Chronicle)
  keys: Wendhope
  content: {{// so:auto}}[State of Wendhope in this campaign. The village is cut off and under nightly attack, roughly fifty people behind a stone wall, running out of arrows and food. Nobody outside knows, because every runner it sent was lost. Its mine is still workable.]
- #3 "Chronicle - Needlehaven" (Adolion Chronicle)
  keys: Needlehaven
  content: [State of Needlehaven in this campaign. {{// so:protect}}The pine forest west of Wendhope is the source of the red fog and the Screechers.{{// so:end}} Its Lord Spirit is awake and in pain, and the forest is thick, alive and growing alabaster where the mine cut its roots.]
- #4 "Chronicle - Driftmere" (Adolion Chronicle)
  keys: Driftmere
  content: {{// so:auto}}[State of Driftmere in this campaign. The mining town is shut: Baroness Serenola has closed the workings, the miners have no income and are running out of savings, and requested Nightriver aid has not arrived. Offerings to Filwern crumble to dust.]
Output one line per change, at most 4:

Then one final line: [why] <one sentence on what changed in the story that made these necessary>
RULES:
- Name each entry by its #number, or by its title exactly as listed above. Anything else is discarded.
- [enable] only an entry marked [currently off]; every other entry is already on.
- [disable] only an entry that is not marked [currently off].
- An entry marked [shown in part — patch only] may only be patched: you have not seen all of it.
- Some entries carry `{{// ...}}` bookkeeping markers. Never write, move or delete a marker, and never change the words between `{{// so:protect}}` and `{{// so:end}}`.
- Prefer [patch] over [rewrite]: quote the first and last words of the span exactly as they appear in the content.
- Keep replacement text under 600 characters. Never restate the whole entry in a patch.
- Only propose a change the story has actually made necessary. Style preferences are not changes.
- Never invent new entries, never touch anything outside the list, never write about the player's own knowledge.
If nothing needs changing, output NONE. That is the expected answer most of the time.
